fatal_errors: The proposed WC-reinforced laser-cladding intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of varying Mo content in an SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
None of the cited evidence establishes that WC creates a lubricious tribo-reactive layer that reduces both friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C.

The predicted 30–50% friction reduction and nearly order-of-magnitude wear reduction are not supported by the cited results; E4 reports increased hardness and a 2.64-fold field weight-loss difference, but no coefficient-of-friction or wide-temperature data.
The hypothesis omits the temperature-dependent lubricant mechanisms central to the target: low-temperature MoS2/Ag films and high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation.
explanation: The response addresses the broad application objective and proposes a controlled comparison with measurable friction, wear, and surface characterization, so it has some problem alignment and experimental discriminability. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, processing route, compositional variable, phase evolution, or tribofilm chemistry. Its baseline is only a generic untreated AlCoCrFeNi alloy, and its service boundaries omit counterface, atmosphere, load, speed, distance, and processing parameters. The evidence supports at most the proposition that WC-reinforced laser-clad HEAs can become harder and more wear resistant. It does not validate self-lubrication, the asserted WC-driven tribocatalytic mechanism, reduced friction, or effectiveness through 800 °C. Consequently, this is an inadequately supported alternative rather than a partial reconstruction.
